WPA2 encryption protects your data in transit. However, encryption alone does not guarantee full network safety.
WPA3 provides the strongest Wi-Fi encryption available. Network-level risks may still apply — see below.
Security type could not be determined. Location services may need to be enabled for detailed analysis.
Even with strong encryption, your connection can still be vulnerable to these attacks:
DNS Hijacking — Attacker redirects your web traffic to malicious sites
Man-in-the-Middle — Attacker intercepts communication between you and the router
Rogue Access Point — Fake Wi-Fi network mimicking a trusted one
